title: 浣溪沙（谁念西风独自凉）
titleEn: Silk-Washing Stream: Who Cares That the West Wind Blows Cold
author: 纳兰性德
intro: A young widower stands alone in the autumn wind and remembers small, happy moments with his late wife. The last line — “back then, I thought it was all just ordinary” — is one of the most quoted lines about loss in Chinese.
analysis: 这是纳兰性德怀念亡妻的词。上阕写现在：秋天的西风吹来，只有他一个人觉得冷，有谁关心呢？黄叶萧萧地落，他关上窗子，在夕阳里站着，想起过去的事。下阕写回忆，用了两个小故事：一是妻子在他喝醉后睡得很沉时，轻轻地不去惊动他；二是用了宋代李清照夫妇的典故（引用古代的故事）——两人比赛记书，说出某件事在哪本书哪一页，赢的人先喝茶，常常笑得把茶泼了，满身茶香。这些都是夫妻之间很平常的小事。最后一句“当时只道是寻常”是全词的重心：当时只觉得这些再普通不过，现在人不在了，才知道那是最珍贵的幸福。这句话说出了很多人的共同感受，所以流传很广。
analysisEn: Nalan Xingde wrote this for his wife, who died young. The first half is the present. The west wind of autumn is blowing, and he alone feels its chill — who cares about that now? Yellow leaves rustle down; he shuts the window and stands in the last light of the setting sun, lost in memories. The second half is the past, told through two tiny scenes. In one, he has drunk too much and is sleeping heavily in spring, and she takes care not to wake him. In the other, they play a game borrowed from the famous Song-dynasty couple Li Qingzhao and her husband: one names a fact, the other must say which book and which page it is on, and the winner drinks tea first — they laughed so hard the tea spilled and the room smelled of it. Bringing in an old story like this is called using an allusion (diǎngù). Neither scene is dramatic; that is the point. The final line, 当时只道是寻常, turns everything: “at the time, I thought it was only ordinary.” Only now, with her gone, does he understand that those ordinary days were the happiness. It is a feeling almost everyone recognises, which is why the line is so often quoted.
background: Nalan Xingde (1655–1685) was a Manchu noble, an imperial bodyguard and the finest ci poet of the Qing dynasty. His wife, Lady Lu, died in 1677 after about three years of marriage; many of his most moving poems mourn her, and this one is traditionally read that way.
pronunciation: 被酒 bèi（醉酒的意思）；春睡重 zhòng；消得 xiāo dé；萧萧 xiāo xiāo。
version: 采用通行版本。“被酒莫惊春睡重”的“被”意思是“为酒所困、醉了”。

lines.py: shuí niàn xī fēng dú zì liáng
lines.lit: Who cares that in the west wind I alone feel cold?
lines.en: Who cares that I stand alone and cold in the west wind?

lines.py: xiāo xiāo huáng yè bì shū chuāng
lines.lit: Rustling yellow leaves; I close the latticed window.
lines.en: Yellow leaves rustle down; I shut the lattice window,

lines.py: chén sī wǎng shì lì cán yáng
lines.lit: Deep in thought on past things, I stand in the fading sun.
lines.en: and stand in the last of the sunlight, thinking of the past.

lines.py: bèi jiǔ mò jīng chūn shuì zhòng
lines.lit: Drunk with wine — “don’t wake him” — deep in spring sleep;
lines.en: When I slept off the wine on spring days, she let me sleep;

lines.py: dǔ shū xiāo dé pō chá xiāng
lines.lit: betting on books, we won the fragrance of spilled tea.
lines.en: we played at quoting books, and laughed until the tea spilled.

lines.py: dāng shí zhǐ dào shì xún cháng
lines.lit: At that time I only said it was ordinary.
lines.en: Back then, I thought it was all just ordinary.

imagery.name: 秋风
imagery.zh: 西风只让他一个人觉得冷，写出妻子去世后的孤独和凄凉。
imagery.en: The west wind chills him alone — the loneliness of a man whose wife is gone.

imagery.name: 叶
imagery.zh: 萧萧黄叶写秋天，也写美好的东西一去不回。
imagery.en: Rustling yellow leaves mark autumn, and things that will never come back.

imagery.name: 夕阳
imagery.zh: 站在残阳里回想往事，一天将尽，正像幸福已经结束。
imagery.en: He remembers the past in the fading sunlight — a day ending, like the happiness that has ended.
